assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organisation as liquid-liquid phase separation, a general physical-chemical principle (phase behaviour, multivalency, interfaces, material properties) that explains membraneless compartments such as P granules and the nucleolus. It created a new concept of molecular organisation that reaches well beyond one system and is the kind of colloid and soft-matter physics I weight highly.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the foundational P-granule and nucleolus demonstrations; Rosen provided the multivalent-interaction framework with minimal reconstituted systems. Pappu and Mittag are strong on sequence-encoded theory and sticker-spacer models, so a three-person limit leaves out real contributors.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade and a half of replication across many systems. Some debate remains about how far in vivo condensates are true thermodynamic phase separation versus other assemblies, and about functional relevance, but the core concept is broadly accepted and recognition looks timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be judged chemistry rather than cell biology or physiology.
Boundary between phase separation as a mechanism and condensates as a descriptive label in vivo.
Fair allocation to theory contributors (Pappu, Mittag) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable cationic lipids and lipid nanoparticles that encapsulate nucleic acids and release them in endosomes are an application of lipid self-assembly, pKa-tuned charge and membrane fusion physics. They enabled siRNA therapeutics and the mRNA vaccines, a lasting and very visible impact with real molecular design principles behind it.
assessment.attribution: Cullis (University of British Columbia) led the lipid and formulation science from early cationic liposomes through ionizable lipids and microfluidic mixing; Anderson contributed combinatorial lipid libraries and in vivo delivery. Hope, MacLachlan, Madden and Langer are credited, and the allocation is contested across academia and industry (patents, companies), so the pair is an informed but uncertain choice.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is extensive, with COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and approved siRNA drugs. The 2023 Medicine prize recognised mRNA nucleoside modification, which may make a chemistry prize on delivery seem partly covered, though it is a distinct chemical invention.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize and perceived category fit.
Credit split between academic and industrial inventors; my recall of the exact roles in the key ionizable lipid optimisations is imperfect.
The supplied credited names omit some key industrial lipid chemists I would otherwise consider.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory with the principle of minimal frustration resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave a statistical-mechanical, funnel-shaped picture of folding, while experimental mapping of transition states (phi-value analysis) tested it quantitatively. This is thermodynamics and kinetics applied to a central biochemical problem, with conceptual clarity and broad influence on protein physics and later on structure prediction and design.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic with Bryngelson are central to the theory; Fersht is decisive on the experimental protein-engineering side. Dill is credited for hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model contributions and could be argued for. A theory-plus-experiment trio is coherent but arguably excludes Bryngelson and Dill.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation; the concept is textbook. Because of the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design, there may be a sense that protein folding has already been recognised, though that was a different problem (prediction and design, not folding mechanism).
uncertainties: Perceived overlap with the 2024 prize.
Fair credit among Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson, Dill and Fersht.
Timeliness: the work is old, so the question is why now.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation converts small-molecule binding into proteasomal destruction, via bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues such as thalidomide analogues acting through cereblon. It created a new pharmacological modality for targets once considered undruggable, with substantial clinical trials under way.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) created the PROTAC concept; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which unlocked the glue mechanism. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim are also meaningful; allocating among PROTAC and glue branches is a real unresolved question and it is a compound discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well confirmed and the field is large, but approval of a PROTAC drug had not yet been established as far as I know, so recognition may be somewhat early on clinical grounds.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug to my knowledge, so maturity is partly pending.
Separate recognition of glue and PROTAC lines may be needed.
Outside my own expertise, so I rely on general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites turned a defect-tolerant, solution-processed semiconductor into photovoltaic absorbers with efficiencies that rose from a few percent to above 25 percent within about a decade, an unusually fast and consequential advance in energy materials, with a rich solid-state chemistry of composition and interfaces.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cells; Park produced the first solid-state, more stable cells; Snaith demonstrated meso-superstructured and thin-film planar devices. Grätzel, Kanatzidis and Seok are strong alternatives, so credit is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Broad independent replication of efficiency, but long-term operational stability and lead toxicity remain unresolved for commercialisation, so some may regard recognition as premature.
uncertainties: Stability and commercial viability not settled.
Contested attribution among six credited names.
Perhaps better regarded as an energy-device advance than a basic chemical concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural and mechanistic work on nitrogenase, the FeMo-cofactor with its interstitial carbide, and the electron-transfer and substrate-binding steps explains biological nitrogen fixation, one of the most important and demanding transformations in chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle supplied the key crystal structures, including the central carbide; Seefeldt and Dean contributed mechanistic and spectroscopic characterisation; Ribbe contributed cofactor biochemistry. The credit is multi-part, and the three-name limit forces choices.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed, but the catalytic mechanism (E4 state, hydride chemistry, N2 binding) is still evolving, so recognition may be somewhat early on mechanism but is mature for structure.
uncertainties: Catalytic mechanism not fully settled.
Weighing structure versus mechanism contributors; this is outside my own field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers of thiols on gold, with soft lithography, brought molecular-level control of interfaces and wetting, and became a foundational platform for surface chemistry, biosensing and microfluidics. This is interfacial and colloid science of the kind the committee has too rarely recognised.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported the first alkanethiolate monolayers on gold; Whitesides developed the broad SAM and soft-lithography programme. Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers are a priority-of-discovery issue. Xia is credited for soft lithography extensions.
assessment.maturity: Concept is very mature and used everywhere; the risk is that recognition is overdue and that the field's headline impact has moved on.
uncertainties: Priority between Sagiv and the thiol-on-gold work.
Whitesides' prominence may overshadow Nuzzo and Allara.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy resolves structure, coupling and ultrafast dynamics of hydrogen bonds, water and peptide or amyloid assemblies on picosecond time scales, extending multidimensional NMR ideas to vibrational motion. It is directly useful in my own field for hydration, membranes and aggregation.
assessment.attribution: Hamm, Tokmakoff and Zanni developed and demonstrated biological and condensed-phase applications; Fleming and Mukamel provide key experimental and theoretical foundations. The theory-versus-experiment split and multi-person credit are unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Technique is mature and widely adopted; recognition of the pioneers could be timely, but a prize for spectroscopy methods competes with many alternatives.
uncertainties: Competing method-based candidates and uncertain priority between theory and experiment.
I may be biased toward this because of field proximity.
